title: BIP identity and lifetime values
description: Identifiers, origins, and lifetime values shared by every BIP message family. Identifiers are opaque domain values: they are never database row numbers, Chromium pointers, renderer routing identifiers, URLs, titles, accessible names, CSS selectors, or array indexes. See the protocol specification section 5 and the domain model section 6.

ProtocolVersion.title: ProtocolVersion
ProtocolVersion.description: Wire protocol version in major.minor form. The current value lives only in bip.version.json; this schema constrains the shape, never the number.

ProfileId.title: ProfileId
ProfileId.description: Opaque browser profile identifier. An incognito profile identifier exists only in memory and is destroyed with its context.

BrowserWindowId.title: BrowserWindowId
BrowserWindowId.description: Opaque browser window identifier, unique within a profile.

TabId.title: TabId
TabId.description: Opaque tab identifier, unique within a profile. A closed tab's identifier is never reassigned.

FrameId.title: FrameId
FrameId.description: Opaque frame identifier, unique within a tab. Every local and out-of-process frame has its own identifier, origin, epoch, revision, and node namespace.

PageEpoch.title: PageEpoch
PageEpoch.description: Opaque page epoch assigned by the browser broker. It changes whenever previously issued semantic handles must not be used for action: committed cross-document navigation, frame or renderer replacement, prerender activation, security-origin transition, broker reconciliation after a crash, an explicit broker invalidation, and back/forward cache restore unless the validation spike proves an equally safe alternative. Compare epochs for equality only; ordering across frames or sessions carries no meaning. Whether back/forward cache restore always allocates a new epoch is [Open (OD-029)].

GraphRevision.title: GraphRevision
GraphRevision.description: Monotonically increasing revision within one active page epoch. It advances whenever a mutation can invalidate a previously observed node, relationship, action precondition, or relevant value. Revisions from different epochs or frames are not comparable.

SemanticNodeId.title: SemanticNodeId
SemanticNodeId.description: Opaque semantic node identifier, unique and non-reused within one FrameId plus PageEpoch. Removing a node permanently retires its identifier for that epoch; a replacement element receives a new identifier even when its selector, text, role, and bounds are unchanged.

SubscriptionId.title: SubscriptionId
SubscriptionId.description: Opaque delta subscription identifier, valid only for one frame endpoint and page epoch.

RequestId.title: RequestId
RequestId.description: Opaque observation request identifier. Exactly one terminal response is delivered per request.

CommandId.title: CommandId
CommandId.description: Opaque one-use renderer command identifier. It is a correlation value, not a capability secret: holding it grants no authority.

DispatchId.title: DispatchId
DispatchId.description: Opaque browser-process dispatch identifier, unique per authorized action envelope.

SnapshotId.title: SnapshotId
SnapshotId.description: Opaque snapshot identifier, unique within a profile session.

TaskId.title: TaskId
TaskId.description: Opaque task identifier owned by the task runtime (domain model section 9).

ActionId.title: ActionId
ActionId.description: Opaque action identifier owned by the task runtime (domain model section 12.1).

SkillVersionId.title: SkillVersionId
SkillVersionId.description: Opaque identifier of the skill version acting as principal (domain model section 10.3).

CapabilityReference.title: CapabilityReference
CapabilityReference.description: Reference to a capability record held by the policy broker. The browser process consumes or marks the capability in flight and never forwards this value to a renderer. It is a reference to a decision record, not a transferable authority token.

ValueReference.title: ValueReference
ValueReference.description: Reference to a value the browser holds, for an action that writes into a field. It is never the value and never carries any part of it, so a proposal naming one discloses nothing about what will be typed — not its length, not its shape, not whether the person has one. Minted by the browser from something a person supplied or confirmed, resolved and spent inside the browser process at dispatch, and never forwarded to a renderer: what reaches a renderer is the resolved text on a one-use command. Page text and model text can never mint one, and a reference the browser does not hold is VALUE_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN rather than an empty field.

ApprovalReceiptReference.title: ApprovalReceiptReference
ApprovalReceiptReference.description: Reference to the approval record that authorized an action. Page text and model text can never mint one.

SensitivityPolicyId.title: SensitivityPolicyId
SensitivityPolicyId.description: Reference to the sensitivity and redaction policy in force for a request. The broker clamps the request to the policy already granted to the task; a request cannot widen it.

EventSequence.title: EventSequence
EventSequence.description: Strictly increasing per-epoch sequence number emitted by a frame endpoint. The broker discards duplicates and out-of-order events; a detected gap invalidates delta state and forces a fresh snapshot.

MonotonicMillis.title: MonotonicMillis
MonotonicMillis.description: A reading of a monotonic clock in milliseconds. BIP carries no wall-clock timestamps, so a message cannot leak browsing time across a trust boundary.

OriginKind.title: OriginKind
OriginKind.description: Whether an origin is a scheme/host/port tuple or an opaque origin. Closed enumeration: a consumer that receives a value outside this list MUST treat the message as unsupported and fail closed, and MUST NOT coerce the value to a known member (protocol section 6.2).

Origin.title: Origin
Origin.description: A normalized security origin recorded by the browser broker at observation time. An opaque origin stays opaque and is never broadened to a predecessor origin; two opaque origins are equal only when their identifiers are equal.

serialization.description: Serialized scheme/host/port for a tuple origin, for example "https://example.test". Absent for an opaque origin.

opaque_id.description: Opaque, session-local identifier distinguishing one opaque origin from another. Present only for an opaque origin, and never a cross-site identifier.

OriginMetadata.title: OriginMetadata
OriginMetadata.description: Browser-owned security context of an observed document. The renderer never supplies these values.

is_potentially_trustworthy.description: Whether Chromium classifies the origin as potentially trustworthy.

is_incognito.description: Whether the owning profile context is incognito. An incognito observation creates no durable record.

DocumentLifecycleState.title: DocumentLifecycleState
DocumentLifecycleState.description: Browser-owned lifecycle state of the observed document. Only ACTIVE is eligible for action. Closed enumeration: a consumer that receives a value outside this list MUST treat the message as unsupported and fail closed, and MUST NOT coerce the value to a known member (protocol section 6.2).

DigestAlgorithm.title: DigestAlgorithm
DigestAlgorithm.description: Digest algorithm used to bind an action proposal to its authorization. Closed enumeration: a consumer that receives a value outside this list MUST treat the message as unsupported and fail closed, and MUST NOT coerce the value to a known member (protocol section 6.2).

ContentDigest.title: ContentDigest
ContentDigest.description: A digest over a canonical encoding of a message. Used to prove that the action authorized is exactly the action proposed.

NodeHandle.title: NodeHandle
NodeHandle.description: The complete reference to one observed semantic node. A node identifier is meaningless without this handle. A handle is ephemeral action input: it may appear in a redacted diagnostic event, but it is unusable once its epoch or document lifecycle ends and it is never a durable reference inside stored evidence.
